Regression 2: Generalised Linear, Quantile and Polynomial Regression¶

Least squares assumes a continuous response with constant noise about a straight-line mean. Three extensions relax this. A generalised linear model handles yes/no outcomes and counts. Quantile regression models a quantile of the response rather than its mean, and resists outliers. Polynomial regression fits curves. After this chapter you can fit each, read what its coefficients mean, and check a fit against an independent condition.

Every program is complete and its output is the output of that program.

Generalised linear models¶

reg::GLMFitResult reg::glm_fit(y, x, reg::GLMOptions options = {}, Config cfg = {});
Series            reg::glm_predict(fit, x_new, reg::GLMPredictionType type = Mean, Config cfg = {});

A GLM says that the mean of y is a function of a linear predictor η = b₀ + b₁x₁ + ..., with a variance that depends on the mean. It is fitted by iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS).

GLMFitResult carries the coefficients with standard errors, z_values, p_values and intervals (normal approximations), fitted_values (the means), linear_predictor, deviance, null_deviance, pseudo_rsquared, dispersion, iterations, converged, log_likelihood, aic, bic. glm_predict returns the mean (Mean, a probability for the binomial family) or the linear predictor (Linear).

  • Logistic and Poisson regression

Quantile regression¶

reg::QuantileFitResult reg::quantile_fit(y, x, reg::QuantileOptions options = {}, Config cfg = {});

It minimises the asymmetric absolute loss, so that a fraction tau of the residuals are below the line. tau = 0.5 is median regression. QuantileOptions has tau, covariance (Robust, the default sandwich estimate, or Iid), alpha, add_intercept, drop_missing, rcond, max_iter (500), tol (1e-7) and eps (a smoothing constant, 1e-6). Standard errors rest on an estimate of the density of the residuals at zero, with the Hall–Sheather bandwidth scaled by the smaller of the standard deviation of y and the interquartile range of the residuals divided by 1.34, so a few outliers do not inflate it; p-values and intervals use Student’s t distribution on the residual degrees of freedom. The result carries coefficients, standard errors, intervals, objective, pseudo_rsquared, iterations and converged.

  • Robust and conditional-quantile fits

Polynomial regression¶

reg::PolyFitResult reg::poly_fit(y, x, reg::PolyOptions options = {}, Config cfg = {});
Series             reg::poly_expand(x, degree, include_cross = false, Config cfg = {});
Series             reg::poly_predict(fit, x_new, Config cfg = {});

PolyOptions::degree is the highest power and include_cross adds products of different predictors. The fit is ordinary least squares on the expanded columns (fit.ols), so everything in Chapter 1 applies; coefficient names show the terms.

  • Curves and cross terms

Checklist¶

  1. Binary outcome: Binomial. Counts: Poisson. Check converged.

  2. Coefficients of a logistic model are log-odds; exponentiate for odds ratios.

  3. Outliers or interest in the spread: quantile regression.

  4. Curves: low-degree polynomials; compare with the information criteria.
